145: ## Auditor execution protocol
146: 
147: The sections below implement the shared requirements. Reviewer identity,
148: fresh packet replay, negative controls, evidence capture and verdict handling
149: are auditor/controller duties; they are not extra mathematical facts for an
150: NL0 author. Mathematical FAIL findings identify the applicable shared table
151: ID and the exact unsupported implication. If the permission boundary itself
152: is ambiguous, disclose that ambiguity rather than silently raising the bar.
153: 
154: Use [self-containment](self-containment.md) and the
155: [audit template](../templates/audit-a.md). New acceptance requires spec/graph
156: v2 and audit v3. Historical PASS records do not satisfy these requirements.
157: 
158: This audit does not use a successful project Lean build as evidence that the
159: NL proof is correct. Querying pinned mathlib for source signatures is allowed;
160: reusing the target's historical Lean proof/verdict requires explicit disclosure
161: and does not establish an independent NL audit.
162: 
163: ## A0. Freeze and disclose
164: 
165: Read the original problem and independently check `spec.json`: target,
166: quantifiers, all H roots, parameter ranges, definitions, representatives,
167: normalization, endpoint conventions, and one-target scope. No H may originate
168: from the proof writer's desired conclusion. Audit target semantics, not just
169: hash equality. Record reviewer/carrier, shared context, read artifacts, and
170: whether any reference solution was seen. Read the canonical graph, not only
171: its generated Markdown. Bind the receipt to spec/graph hashes.
172: Generate the exhaustive global index with
173: `python3 nl0/scripts/nl0.py overview nl0.json --spec spec.json --out global-overview.json`.
174: It preserves every actual H (including unused or late-appended H), full global
175: statements/definitions and dependency edges with canonical pointers and hashes.
176: Read this inventory before claiming a node/condition is absent; a partial line
177: page cannot establish absence. The index supplies no verdict and does not
178: replace inspection of the relevant canonical proof and primary-source content.
179: The clean test adapter uses this same core generator, not a separate inventory
180: or mathematical standard.
181: Original-problem/source fidelity and local proof validity are separate tasks.
182: The original text may be read for target and citation checks; it may not fill
183: missing content during per-R packet-only replay. Record the actual boundary.
184: Check that original conditions really are H nodes, rather than predicates
185: hidden in a globally visible parameter type. A prime/nonzero condition,
186: characteristic constraint, range or equation must not become available to an
187: R with empty inputs through that encoding. Matching the full closed theorem

190: ## A1. Definitions and notation
191: 
192: For each D record a verdict with a concrete explanation. Check unique meaning,
193: type/domain, global versus local binding, definition dependencies, construction
194: or existence prerequisites, and applicability at every use. A guarded symbol
195: must not supply its own prerequisite. Record arbitrary choices, parameter
196: dependencies, and equivalence to the original definition. No project theorem
197: may hide as a definition, record field, predicate, or typeclass assumption.

199: Reverse-check every actual mathematical object occurrence against a legitimate
200: declaration. Inspect local introduction position, first use, type/domain,
201: basis and end scope. Input-bound variables are not free locals; witnesses need
202: proved existence. Merely checking registered symbol names misses unregistered
203: ones. Definitions cannot smuggle properties or extra ancestor statements.

205: ## A2. Sources

208: probe, not merely a `#check` name or a search result. Confirm declaration kind,

A sphere-valued map cannot vanish outside a compact set. As approved by
the user on 2026-10-23, interpret spatial compact support as compact support
of a perturbation from a **fixed unit vector**, locally uniformly in time.
This is a disclosed nontrivial interpretation, not a claimed author-issued
correction.

Let \(n,m\geq1\) be integers and let
\(u:\mathbb R^n\times(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R^m\) be jointly smooth.
Fix \(q\in\mathbb R^m\) with \(|q|=1\). Assume:

1. \(|u(x,t)|=1\) for all \(x\) and \(t>0\).
2. The acceleration \(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu\) is normal to the sphere at
   \(u\): at each point there is a real scalar \(a(x,t)\) with
   \(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu=a u\). No regularity of the selected scalar is
   assumed.
3. For every \(0<s<t<\infty\), a compact set
   \(C_{[s,t]}\subset\mathbb R^n\) exists such that \(u(x,r)=q\) for
   \(x\notin C_{[s,t]}\), \(r\in[s,t]\).

With Euclidean norms and Lebesgue measure, define

\[
e(x,t)=|u_t(x,t)|^2+\sum_{j=1}^n|\partial_{x_j}u(x,t)|^2,
\qquad E(t)=\int_{\mathbb R^n}e(x,t)\,dx.
\]

The spatial gradient square is the Frobenius square, and
\(\Delta_xu=\sum_j\partial_{x_jx_j}u\) component by component.
Prove integrability of \(e(\cdot,t)\), differentiability of \(E\),
and \(E'(t)=0\) for every \(t>0\). No assertion at time zero is required.

spec.full_target:
A sphere-valued map cannot vanish outside a compact set. As approved by
the user on 2026-10-23, interpret spatial compact support as compact support
of a perturbation from a **fixed unit vector**, locally uniformly in time.
This is a disclosed nontrivial interpretation, not a claimed author-issued
correction.

Let \(n,m\geq1\) be integers and let
\(u:\mathbb R^n\times(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R^m\) be jointly smooth.
Fix \(q\in\mathbb R^m\) with \(|q|=1\). Assume:

1. \(|u(x,t)|=1\) for all \(x\) and \(t>0\).
2. The acceleration \(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu\) is normal to the sphere at
   \(u\): at each point there is a real scalar \(a(x,t)\) with
   \(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu=a u\). No regularity of the selected scalar is
   assumed.
3. For every \(0<s<t<\infty\), a compact set
   \(C_{[s,t]}\subset\mathbb R^n\) exists such that \(u(x,r)=q\) for
   \(x\notin C_{[s,t]}\), \(r\in[s,t]\).

With Euclidean norms and Lebesgue measure, define

\[
e(x,t)=|u_t(x,t)|^2+\sum_{j=1}^n|\partial_{x_j}u(x,t)|^2,
\qquad E(t)=\int_{\mathbb R^n}e(x,t)\,dx.
\]

The spatial gradient square is the Frobenius square, and
\(\Delta_xu=\sum_j\partial_{x_jx_j}u\) component by component.
Prove integrability of \(e(\cdot,t)\), differentiability of \(E\),
and \(E'(t)=0\) for every \(t>0\). No assertion at time zero is required.
spec.conclusion: For every r>0 the function x↦e(x,r) is Lebesgue integrable on V; E is differentiable on (0,∞), and E'(r)=0 for every r>0. In particular E(s)=E(t) for all s,t>0. The energy is ∫_V (|u_t|^2+sum_{j=1}^n|u_j|^2) dx, with no factor 1/2 and no assertion at time zero.

argument.text: Fix x∈V and r>0. H002 supplies continuous derivatives of every order near (x,r). H004 implies u·u=1. Apply M001 to the square of each real component of the time curve ρ↦u(x,ρ) and add the m derivatives. Differentiating this constant identity gives 2sum_{k=1}^m u_k (u_t)_k=2u·u_t=0, hence u·u_t=0. Since the time and point were arbitrary this identity holds on the entire open domain.

produces.statement: For every y∈V and ρ>0, u(y,ρ)·u_t(y,ρ)=0.

argument.text: Choose the pointwise scalar a using H005. Dot u_tt−Δu=a u with u_t. By F001 and symmetry of the real dot product, u_t·(u_tt−Δu)=a(u_t·u)=0. This uses only the value of a at the chosen point, with no differentiation or regularity of a.

produces.statement: u_t(x,r)·(u_tt(x,r)−Δu(x,r))=0.

argument.text: Differentiate the identity in F001 in time, using M001 on each component product and H002 to supply both derivatives: |u_t|^2+u·u_tt=0. For a spatial index j, differentiating u·u=1 in x_j by M001 first gives u·u_j=0 at every point. Differentiate that identity once more in x_j, again by M001, to obtain |u_j|^2+u·u_jj=0. These finite component sums establish u·u_tt=−|u_t|^2 and u·u_jj=−|u_j|^2 for every j.

produces.statement: u(x,r)·u_tt(x,r)=−|u_t(x,r)|^2, and for every 1≤i≤n, u(x,r)·u_ii(x,r)=−|u_i(x,r)|^2, where u_i and u_ii are the i-indexed members of the globally defined families u_j and u_jj.

argument.text: Dot the chosen normality equation with u. H004 gives |u|^2=1; F003 and Δu=sum_j u_jj therefore give a=u·(u_tt−Δu)=sum_j|u_j|^2−|u_t|^2. The same calculation applies to any real scalar satisfying that equation, hence gives the claimed universally conditional scalar formula. Substituting it back gives the explicit wave-map equation. F001, F002 and F003 give all remaining clauses. Generalize over x and r; the existentially selected scalar does not escape.

argument.text: Fix t0>0 and put J=[t0/2,3t0/2]. Its endpoints satisfy 0<t0/2<3t0/2, so H006 supplies a compact spatial set C on whose complement u=q for every time in J. Compact sets in Euclidean space are closed; hence (V\C)×int J is open. At each of its points u agrees with the constant q on a neighborhood. Every positive-order derivative is therefore zero there: difference quotients of a locally constant function are zero, and this applies successively to all orders. H002 gives continuity of all derivatives on the entire open domain.
Apply M009 to the compact set C and the identity map V→V. The identity is continuous, so it gives a real uniform norm bound even when C is empty.

produces.statement: There exists a real L with |x|≤L for all x∈C.

argument.text: Choose L with the bound of F001 and set R=max(L,0)+1>0 and Q=[−R,R]^n. For x∈C, every coordinate satisfies |x_j|≤|x|≤L<R, so C⊂(−R,R)^n=int Q. H001 gives positive finite dimensions; Q is a compact measurable coordinate box. M010 with all lower endpoints −R and upper endpoints R gives |Q|=∏_{j=1}^n(2R)=(2R)^n<∞.

produces.statement: R>0, Q=[−R,R]^n is compact and measurable, C⊂int Q, |Q|=(2R)^n<∞, and all positive-order derivatives of u vanish on (V\C)×int J.

argument.text: Fix r∈int J. Smoothness in H002 and the finite component formulas defining e,A,B_j,T_j,g_j imply continuity of these functions and of e_t and ∂_{x_j}g_j. The zero derivatives proved in S001 make all of these sections zero outside C. Their nonzero sets have closures contained in the closed compact set C, so each has compact support. Apply M003 to each section with X=V, Z=R and μ=dx: Euclidean Borel open sets are measurable, and Lebesgue measure is finite on compact sets. Thus every listed section is integrable. Apply M009 on Q to each continuous scalar section to obtain a finite absolute bound on Q; together with zero values off Q, the usual absolute integral bound is that constant times |Q|. This also proves the supplied bounded-support estimate.

produces.statement: For every ρ∈int J, all sections e(·,ρ), e_t(·,ρ), A(·,ρ), B_i(·,ρ), T_i(·,ρ), g_i(·,ρ), ∂_{x_i}g_i(·,ρ), for 1≤i≤n, are continuous, compactly supported in C, integrable, and have an absolute integral bounded by a finite uniform-in-space bound times |Q|.

argument.text: Since V\C is open and contains ∂Q, every section in F003 vanishes on a neighborhood of ∂Q. The time t0 belongs to int J, so e(·,t0) is integrable. Generalize over the arbitrary t0. The same argument supplies the complete existential common-support assertion and all bounds in N002 for each t0; in particular it proves integrability at every positive time.

argument.text: Fix x∈V, r>0 and a spatial index j. By H002 every derivative entering u_t,u_tt,u_j,u_jj,u_jt is continuous and has derivatives of every order. Their finite sums and component products, in particular e and g_j, are jointly smooth by the usual finite differentiation rules.

argument.text: Define U(y,ρ)=u(y,ρ) for ρ>0 and zero for ρ≤0. Near (x,r) it agrees with u since r>0. H002 gives that U is C^2 at this point. Apply M002 over R to U at (x,r), with smoothness order 2; the real minimum smoothness is 2. Evaluate the symmetric second derivative on the time direction (0,1) and the jth spatial coordinate direction. Coordinate directional derivatives are the corresponding partial derivatives, so ∂_r u_j(x,r)=∂_{x_j}u_t(x,r)=u_jt(x,r). This works at every positive time and point.

produces.statement: For every y∈V, ρ>0 and 1≤i≤n, ∂_ρ u_i(y,ρ)=u_it(y,ρ), where u_it is the i-indexed member of u_jt.

argument.text: Apply M001 over R to each squared component of u_t in the time variable and to each squared component of u_j in the time variable. Add the finitely many component derivatives and use F002 to replace ∂_r u_j by u_jt. This yields e_t=2u_t·u_tt+2sum_{i=1}^n u_i·u_it=2A+2sum_{i=1}^n B_i. Apply M001 to each component product in g_j along the x_j-coordinate line: ∂_{x_j}g_j=u_jt·u_j+u_t·u_jj=B_j+T_j. F001 gives continuity of all terms. Generalize over x,r,j to obtain the complete N003.

argument.text: Fix t0>0. Choose C,R from N002 and use its J=[t0/2,3t0/2], Q=[−R,R]^n. Put η=t0/4>0 and I=[t0−η,t0+η]⊂int J. N003 makes e_t continuous on Q×I. This product is compact, since Q and the closed bounded interval I are compact.
Apply M009 to the continuous scalar function e_t on the compact product Q×I. It gives a real finite bound L for |e_t| on this product.

produces.statement: There exists L∈R such that |e_t(y,ρ)|≤L for every y∈Q and ρ∈I.

argument.text: Choose L from F001 and put K=max(L,0)≥0. For 0<|h|<η and any fixed y∈Q, apply M005 to ρ↦e(y,ρ) on [t0,t0+h] if h>0, and on [t0+h,t0] if h<0. These nondegenerate intervals lie in I, the function is smooth there by N003, and its derivative is e_t with absolute value at most K by F001. The within-interval derivative agrees with the ordinary derivative on these intervals. The resulting estimate is |e(y,t0+h)−e(y,t0)|≤K|h|, hence the absolute quotient is at most K. For y∉Q, both densities are zero by N002, since both times belong to int J. Therefore the quotient is bounded on V by K 1_Q.

produces.statement: For every nonzero ζ with |ζ|<η and every y∈V, |(e(y,t0+ζ)−e(y,t0))/ζ|≤K 1_Q(y).

argument.text: Define Φ(ζ,y) to be this quotient when 0<|ζ|<η and zero otherwise, and define β=K1_Q. For those small nonzero ζ each quotient is continuous in y, hence strongly measurable, and is integrable as a linear combination of the two integrable density sections supplied by N002. N002 gives measurable Q with finite measure. The nonnegative simple function β has integral K|Q|<∞, so it is integrable. N003 gives pointwise convergence Φ(ζ,y)→e_t(y,t0) as ζ→0 through nonzero values, by the definition of the derivative of e(y,·). F002 is the required domination.

produces.statement: Along the punctured real neighborhood filter at zero, Φ(ζ,·) is eventually strongly measurable and integrable, |Φ(ζ,y)|≤β(y) for all y, β is integrable, and Φ(ζ,y)→e_t(y,t0) for every y∈V.

argument.text: Apply M004 with X=V, μ=dx, Z=R, index set R and the punctured neighborhood filter at zero. F003 supplies measurability, domination, integrability of the bound and pointwise, therefore almost-everywhere, convergence. Thus ∫_V Φ(ζ,y)dy tends to ∫_V e_t(y,t0)dy.

produces.statement: lim_{ζ→0,ζ≠0} ∫_V Φ(ζ,y)dy = ∫_V e_t(y,t0)dy.

argument.text: For 0<|ζ|<η the two density sections are integrable by N002. M013, applied to e(·,t0+ζ) and −e(·,t0), and M014 with scalars −1 and 1/ζ give ∫_V Φ(ζ,y)dy=(E(t0+ζ)−E(t0))/ζ. Here E is legitimate because N002 proved integrability at every positive time, and t0+ζ>0. Substituting into F004 proves differentiability of the actual energy and E'(t0)=∫_V e_t(y,t0)dy. Generalize over t0>0.

argument.text: Define Xhat to be the tuple space of all coordinates except j with product Lebesgue measure, and χ(x)=((x_i)_{i≠j},x_j). Apply M011 with predicate i≠j to split the finite product measure. The remaining block {j} has a unique element; M017 identifies its product measure with ordinary one-dimensional Lebesgue measure by evaluation at j. Composing these explicit measurable equivalences shows that χ is a measure-preserving measurable equivalence from V to Xhat×R. The inverse is coordinate insertion. When n=1, Xhat is the one-point empty product with mass one, so the same identification applies.

produces.statement: χ:V→Xhat×R and its inverse are measurable, χ is bijective and preserves dx and the product of the Lebesgue measures on Xhat and R.

argument.text: Fix any y∈Xhat and define G(z)=g_j(χ^{-1}(y,z),t0). By N003 this function is smooth and G'(z)=∂_{x_j}g_j(χ^{-1}(y,z),t0). If z=±R, the inserted point lies outside C, since C⊂(−R,R)^n; hence G(−R)=G(R)=0. The derivative is continuous on the finite interval [−R,R], so it is interval integrable there. M006 gives ∫_{−R}^R G'(z)dz=G(R)−G(−R)=0. This is also the integral on the closed interval: its endpoints have Lebesgue measure zero. For |z|>R the derivative vanishes by F001; thus ∫_R ∂_{x_j}g_j(χ^{-1}(y,z),t0) dz=0. This proves the zero inner integral for every y, including when some other coordinate lies outside the box.

produces.statement: For every y∈Xhat, the function z↦∂_{x_j}g_j(χ^{-1}(y,z),t0) is integrable on R and its integral over R, equivalently over [−R,R], is zero.

argument.text: Define H(y,z)=∂_{x_j}g_j(χ^{-1}(y,z),t0). It is continuous and supported in the compact product box corresponding to Q, hence integrable; equivalently integrability follows by transport through the measure-preserving measurable equivalence in F002 from F001. Apply M016 with the coordinate equivalence χ and scalar function H: ∫_V ∂_{x_j}g_j(x,t0)dx=∫_{Xhat×R}H. Apply M007 to this integrable H. The product Lebesgue factors are sigma-finite, hence s-finite, including the empty factor. F003 makes each inner integral zero. Therefore ∫_V ∂_{x_j}g_j(x,t0)dx=∫_{Xhat}0=0. Restricting to Q gives the identical box integral, since its integrand vanishes off Q. This is precisely the coordinate FTC/Fubini integration-by-parts step.

Integrate the identity in F001 and use M013 with its two integrable summands B_j(·,t0),T_j(·,t0). F004 yields 0=∫_V B_j+∫_V T_j. Rearranging gives ∫_V B_j=−∫_V T_j. Unfold the definitions of B and T to get exactly the asserted vector-dot-product formula. Generalize over t0>0 and all spatial indices j.

argument.text: Use M013 for the two terms in e_t, M014 to take the factors 2 outside the integrals, and M012 for the finite sum of integrable B_j sections. Then use N005 for every j. This retains the exact calculation E'(t0)=2∫_V u_t·u_tt dx+2sum_j∫_V u_j·u_jt dx=2∫_V u_t·u_tt dx−2sum_j∫_V u_t·u_jj dx. Every integral is finite by F001.

argument.text: Apply M012 also to the finite family T_j and use M013 and M014 with scalar −1 to combine the difference of integrals. By finite distributivity of the dot product and Δu=sum_j u_jj, A−sum_j T_j=u_t·(u_tt−Δu) pointwise. Thus F002 becomes E'(t0)=2∫_V u_t(x,t0)·(u_tt(x,t0)−Δu(x,t0))dx. N001 makes this integrand zero at every x, so its integral and E'(t0) are zero.

The time t0 was arbitrary. N002 gives integrability for every positive time, N004 gives differentiability on (0,∞), and F003 gives the zero derivative there. The definitions e=|u_t|^2+sum_j|u_j|^2 and E=∫e preserve the required energy normalization without a factor 1/2.

argument.text: For completeness fix arbitrary s,t>0. If s<t, restrict E to [s,t]; F004 gives differentiability there and within derivative equal to its ordinary derivative zero. M005 with bound 0 gives |E(t)−E(s)|≤0(t−s)=0, hence E(t)=E(s). If t<s, apply the same argument on [t,s], and if s=t equality is immediate. The source expects a total real function: extend E arbitrarily outside (0,∞); it agrees with E on an open neighborhood of either closed interval, so its derivatives there are unchanged. Generalizing over s,t gives constancy. Together with F004 this proves every clause of P. All arguments concern positive times only.

original_context.full_target:
A sphere-valued map cannot vanish outside a compact set. As approved by
the user on 2026-10-23, interpret spatial compact support as compact support
of a perturbation from a **fixed unit vector**, locally uniformly in time.
This is a disclosed nontrivial interpretation, not a claimed author-issued
correction.

Let \(n,m\geq1\) be integers and let
\(u:\mathbb R^n\times(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R^m\) be jointly smooth.
Fix \(q\in\mathbb R^m\) with \(|q|=1\). Assume:

1. \(|u(x,t)|=1\) for all \(x\) and \(t>0\).
2. The acceleration \(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu\) is normal to the sphere at
   \(u\): at each point there is a real scalar \(a(x,t)\) with
   \(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu=a u\). No regularity of the selected scalar is
   assumed.
3. For every \(0<s<t<\infty\), a compact set
   \(C_{[s,t]}\subset\mathbb R^n\) exists such that \(u(x,r)=q\) for
   \(x\notin C_{[s,t]}\), \(r\in[s,t]\).

With Euclidean norms and Lebesgue measure, define

\[
e(x,t)=|u_t(x,t)|^2+\sum_{j=1}^n|\partial_{x_j}u(x,t)|^2,
\qquad E(t)=\int_{\mathbb R^n}e(x,t)\,dx.
\]

The spatial gradient square is the Frobenius square, and
\(\Delta_xu=\sum_j\partial_{x_jx_j}u\) component by component.
Prove integrability of \(e(\cdot,t)\), differentiability of \(E\),
and \(E'(t)=0\) for every \(t>0\). No assertion at time zero is required.

hypotheses.statement: n and m are integers with n≥1 and m≥1 (represented as natural-number dimensions).
u:R^n×(0,∞)→R^m is jointly smooth: every finite-order coordinate partial derivative exists and is continuous on this open domain.
q∈R^m is fixed and |q|=1.
For every x∈R^n and every r>0, |u(x,r)|=1.
For every x∈R^n and every r>0 there exists a real scalar a with u_tt(x,r)−Δu(x,r)=a u(x,r). No regularity or globally chosen scalar field is assumed.
For every pair of real numbers 0<s<t<∞ there exists a compact set C_[s,t]⊂R^n such that u(x,r)=q for every x∉C_[s,t] and every r∈[s,t].

original_context.conclusion: For every r>0 the function x↦e(x,r) is Lebesgue integrable on V; E is differentiable on (0,∞), and E'(r)=0 for every r>0. In particular E(s)=E(t) for all s,t>0. The energy is ∫_V (|u_t|^2+sum_{j=1}^n|u_j|^2) dx, with no factor 1/2 and no assertion at time zero.

argument.text: Define Xhat to be the tuple space of all coordinates except j with product Lebesgue measure, and χ(x)=((x_i)_{i≠j},x_j). Apply M011 with predicate i≠j to split the finite product measure. The remaining block {j} has a unique element; M017 identifies its product measure with ordinary one-dimensional Lebesgue measure by evaluation at j. Composing these explicit measurable equivalences shows that χ is a measure-preserving measurable equivalence from V to Xhat×R. The inverse is coordinate insertion. When n=1, Xhat is the one-point empty product with mass one, so the same identification applies.

argument.text: Fix any y∈Xhat and define G(z)=g_j(χ^{-1}(y,z),t0). By N003 this function is smooth and G'(z)=∂_{x_j}g_j(χ^{-1}(y,z),t0). If z=±R, the inserted point lies outside C, since C⊂(−R,R)^n; hence G(−R)=G(R)=0. The derivative is continuous on the finite interval [−R,R], so it is interval integrable there. M006 gives ∫_{−R}^R G'(z)dz=G(R)−G(−R)=0. This is also the integral on the closed interval: its endpoints have Lebesgue measure zero. For |z|>R the derivative vanishes by F001; thus ∫_R ∂_{x_j}g_j(χ^{-1}(y,z),t0) dz=0. This proves the zero inner integral for every y, including when some other coordinate lies outside the box.

argument.text: Define H(y,z)=∂_{x_j}g_j(χ^{-1}(y,z),t0). It is continuous and supported in the compact product box corresponding to Q, hence integrable; equivalently integrability follows by transport through the measure-preserving measurable equivalence in F002 from F001. Apply M016 with the coordinate equivalence χ and scalar function H: ∫_V ∂_{x_j}g_j(x,t0)dx=∫_{Xhat×R}H. Apply M007 to this integrable H. The product Lebesgue factors are sigma-finite, hence s-finite, including the empty factor. F003 makes each inner integral zero. Therefore ∫_V ∂_{x_j}g_j(x,t0)dx=∫_{Xhat}0=0. Restricting to Q gives the identical box integral, since its integrand vanishes off Q. This is precisely the coordinate FTC/Fubini integration-by-parts step.

original_context.full_target:
A sphere-valued map cannot vanish outside a compact set. As approved by
the user on 2026-10-23, interpret spatial compact support as compact support
of a perturbation from a **fixed unit vector**, locally uniformly in time.
This is a disclosed nontrivial interpretation, not a claimed author-issued
correction.

Let \(n,m\geq1\) be integers and let
\(u:\mathbb R^n\times(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R^m\) be jointly smooth.
Fix \(q\in\mathbb R^m\) with \(|q|=1\). Assume:

1. \(|u(x,t)|=1\) for all \(x\) and \(t>0\).
2. The acceleration \(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu\) is normal to the sphere at
   \(u\): at each point there is a real scalar \(a(x,t)\) with
   \(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu=a u\). No regularity of the selected scalar is
   assumed.
3. For every \(0<s<t<\infty\), a compact set
   \(C_{[s,t]}\subset\mathbb R^n\) exists such that \(u(x,r)=q\) for
   \(x\notin C_{[s,t]}\), \(r\in[s,t]\).

With Euclidean norms and Lebesgue measure, define

\[
e(x,t)=|u_t(x,t)|^2+\sum_{j=1}^n|\partial_{x_j}u(x,t)|^2,
\qquad E(t)=\int_{\mathbb R^n}e(x,t)\,dx.
\]

The spatial gradient square is the Frobenius square, and
\(\Delta_xu=\sum_j\partial_{x_jx_j}u\) component by component.
Prove integrability of \(e(\cdot,t)\), differentiability of \(E\),
and \(E'(t)=0\) for every \(t>0\). No assertion at time zero is required.

argument.text: Fix x∈V, r>0 and a spatial index j. By H002 every derivative entering u_t,u_tt,u_j,u_jj,u_jt is continuous and has derivatives of every order. Their finite sums and component products, in particular e and g_j, are jointly smooth by the usual finite differentiation rules.

argument.text: Define U(y,ρ)=u(y,ρ) for ρ>0 and zero for ρ≤0. Near (x,r) it agrees with u since r>0. H002 gives that U is C^2 at this point. Apply M002 over R to U at (x,r), with smoothness order 2; the real minimum smoothness is 2. Evaluate the symmetric second derivative on the time direction (0,1) and the jth spatial coordinate direction. Coordinate directional derivatives are the corresponding partial derivatives, so ∂_r u_j(x,r)=∂_{x_j}u_t(x,r)=u_jt(x,r). This works at every positive time and point.

produces.statement: For every y∈V, ρ>0 and 1≤i≤n, ∂_ρ u_i(y,ρ)=u_it(y,ρ), where u_it is the i-indexed member of u_jt.

argument.text: Extend each time curve below by zero at nonpositive times; this does not change it near the chosen r>0. Apply M001 over R to each squared component of u_t in the time variable and to each squared component of u_j in the time variable. Add the finitely many component derivatives and use F002 to replace ∂_r u_j by u_jt. This yields e_t=2u_t·u_tt+2sum_{i=1}^n u_i·u_it=2A+2sum_{i=1}^n B_i. argument.text: Fix t0>0 and 1≤j≤n. Choose C,R from N002 and put Q=[−R,R]^n. At t0, g_j, its jth derivative and the two summands B_j,T_j are continuous, integrable, and zero outside C⊂int Q. N003 gives smoothness and the pointwise identity ∂_{x_j}g_j=B_j+T_j.

argument.text: Define Xhat to be the tuple space of all coordinates except j with product Lebesgue measure, and χ(x)=((x_i)_{i≠j},x_j). Apply M011 with predicate i≠j to split the finite product measure. The remaining block {j} has a unique element; M017 identifies its product measure with ordinary one-dimensional Lebesgue measure by evaluation at j. Composing these explicit measurable equivalences shows that χ is a measure-preserving measurable equivalence from V to Xhat×R. The inverse is coordinate insertion. When n=1, Xhat is the one-point empty product with mass one, so the same identification applies.

produces.statement: χ:V→Xhat×R and its inverse are measurable, χ is bijective and preserves dx and the product of the Lebesgue measures on Xhat and R.

argument.text: Fix any y∈Xhat and define G(z)=g_j(χ^{-1}(y,z),t0). By N003 this function is smooth and G'(z)=∂_{x_j}g_j(χ^{-1}(y,z),t0). If z=±R, the inserted point lies outside C, since C⊂(−R,R)^n; hence G(−R)=G(R)=0. The derivative is continuous on the finite interval [−R,R], so it is interval integrable there. M006 gives ∫_{−R}^R G'(z)dz=G(R)−G(−R)=0. This is also the integral on the closed interval: its endpoints have Lebesgue measure zero. For |z|>R the derivative vanishes by F001; thus ∫_{z∈ℝ} ∂_{x_j}g_j(χ^{-1}(y,z),t0) dz=0. This proves the zero inner integral for every y, including when some other coordinate lies outside the box.

produces.statement: For every y0∈Xhat, the function z↦∂_{x_j}g_j(χ^{-1}(y0,z),t0) is integrable on the real line and its integral over the real line, equivalently over [−R,R], is zero.

argument.text: Define H(y,z)=∂_{x_j}g_j(χ^{-1}(y,z),t0). It is continuous by N003 and the explicit coordinate insertion map, and vanishes outside the compact product box corresponding to Q by F001. Thus its support closure is compact. Apply M003 on Xhat×R with its product Lebesgue measure to obtain integrability. Apply M016 with the coordinate equivalence χ and scalar function H: ∫_V ∂_{x_j}g_j(x,t0)dx=∫_{Xhat×R}H. Apply M007 to this integrable H. The product Lebesgue factors are sigma-finite, hence s-finite, including the empty factor. F003 makes each inner integral zero. Therefore ∫_V ∂_{x_j}g_j(x,t0)dx=∫_{Xhat}0=0. Restricting to Q gives the identical box integral, since its integrand vanishes off Q. This is precisely the coordinate FTC/Fubini integration-by-parts step.

Integrate the identity in F001 and use M013 with its two integrable summands B_j(·,t0),T_j(·,t0). F004 yields 0=∫_V B_j+∫_V T_j. Rearranging gives ∫_V B_j=−∫_V T_j. Unfold the definitions of B and T to get exactly the asserted vector-dot-product formula. Generalize over t0>0 and all spatial indices j.

original_context.full_target:
A sphere-valued map cannot vanish outside a compact set. As approved by
the user on 2026-10-23, interpret spatial compact support as compact support
of a perturbation from a **fixed unit vector**, locally uniformly in time.
This is a disclosed nontrivial interpretation, not a claimed author-issued
correction.

Let \(n,m\geq1\) be integers and let
\(u:\mathbb R^n\times(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R^m\) be jointly smooth.
Fix \(q\in\mathbb R^m\) with \(|q|=1\). Assume:

1. \(|u(x,t)|=1\) for all \(x\) and \(t>0\).
2. The acceleration \(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu\) is normal to the sphere at
   \(u\): at each point there is a real scalar \(a(x,t)\) with
   \(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu=a u\). No regularity of the selected scalar is
   assumed.
3. For every \(0<s<t<\infty\), a compact set
   \(C_{[s,t]}\subset\mathbb R^n\) exists such that \(u(x,r)=q\) for
   \(x\notin C_{[s,t]}\), \(r\in[s,t]\).

With Euclidean norms and Lebesgue measure, define

\[
e(x,t)=|u_t(x,t)|^2+\sum_{j=1}^n|\partial_{x_j}u(x,t)|^2,
\qquad E(t)=\int_{\mathbb R^n}e(x,t)\,dx.
\]

The spatial gradient square is the Frobenius square, and
\(\Delta_xu=\sum_j\partial_{x_jx_j}u\) component by component.
Prove integrability of \(e(\cdot,t)\), differentiability of \(E\),
and \(E'(t)=0\) for every \(t>0\). No assertion at time zero is required.

hypotheses.statement: n and m are integers with n≥1 and m≥1 (represented as natural-number dimensions).
u:R^n×(0,∞)→R^m is jointly smooth: every finite-order coordinate partial derivative exists and is continuous on this open domain.
q∈R^m is fixed and |q|=1.
For every x∈R^n and every r>0, |u(x,r)|=1.
For every x∈R^n and every r>0 there exists a real scalar a with u_tt(x,r)−Δu(x,r)=a u(x,r). No regularity or globally chosen scalar field is assumed.
For every pair of real numbers 0<s<t<∞ there exists a compact set C_[s,t]⊂R^n such that u(x,r)=q for every x∉C_[s,t] and every r∈[s,t].

original_context.conclusion: For every r>0 the function x↦e(x,r) is Lebesgue integrable on V; E is differentiable on (0,∞), and E'(r)=0 for every r>0. In particular E(s)=E(t) for all s,t>0. The energy is ∫_V (|u_t|^2+sum_{j=1}^n|u_j|^2) dx, with no factor 1/2 and no assertion at time zero.

This is a disclosed nontrivial interpretation, not a claimed author-issued
correction.

Let \(n,m\geq1\) be integers and let
\(u:\mathbb R^n\times(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R^m\) be jointly smooth.
Fix \(q\in\mathbb R^m\) with \(|q|=1\). Assume:

1. \(|u(x,t)|=1\) for all \(x\) and \(t>0\).
2. The acceleration \(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu\) is normal to the sphere at
   \(u\): at each point there is a real scalar \(a(x,t)\) with
   \(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu=a u\). No regularity of the selected scalar is
   assumed.
3. For every \(0<s<t<\infty\), a compact set
   \(C_{[s,t]}\subset\mathbb R^n\) exists such that \(u(x,r)=q\) for
   \(x\notin C_{[s,t]}\), \(r\in[s,t]\).

With Euclidean norms and Lebesgue measure, define

\[
e(x,t)=|u_t(x,t)|^2+\sum_{j=1}^n|\partial_{x_j}u(x,t)|^2,
\qquad E(t)=\int_{\mathbb R^n}e(x,t)\,dx.
\]

The spatial gradient square is the Frobenius square, and
\(\Delta_xu=\sum_j\partial_{x_jx_j}u\) component by component.
Prove integrability of \(e(\cdot,t)\), differentiability of \(E\),
and \(E'(t)=0\) for every \(t>0\). No assertion at time zero is required.

u:R^n×(0,∞)→R^m is jointly smooth: every finite-order coordinate partial derivative exists and is continuous on this open domain.
q∈R^m is fixed and |q|=1.
